function.name: client_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates of a single client based on the client's name and the status of the mandate. Partners can use this API to retrieve mandate information for their clients. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the client whose mandates are to be fetched.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If not specified, mandates with all statuses are retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches all mandates for all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the status of the mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of mandates to fetch. Possible values are 'active', 'pending', and 'inactive'.

function.name: partner_sips
function.description: Fetch all Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) of all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the given status of the SIP. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the SIPs to be fetched. Valid statuses include 'active', 'stopped', and 'paused'.

message.content:
A **mandate** in the context of financial services (especially in wealth management, investment advisory, or banking) refers to a formal authorization that a client gives to a financial professional or institution to act on their behalf in managing their investments or financial affairs. Key points about a mandate: | Aspect | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Grants the advisor or institution the legal authority to make investment decisions, execute trades, manage portfolios, or perform other financial actions for the client. | | **Types** | • **Active Mandate** – The advisor is actively managing the client’s portfolio.
• **Pending Mandate** – The mandate has been agreed upon but is awaiting activation (e.g., waiting for funds to be transferred).
• **Inactive Mandate** – The mandate has been terminated or paused. | | **Components** | • **Client Information** – Name, contact details, risk profile.
• **Mandate Status** – Active, pending, inactive.
• **Scope of Authority** – What the advisor can do (e.g., buy/sell securities, rebalance, set investment limits). | | **Legal Basis** | Usually documented in a signed agreement or contract that complies with regulatory requirements (e.g., MiFID II in Europe, SEC rules in the U.S.). | | **Benefits for Clients** | • Professional management of assets.
• Access to expertise and research.
• Potential for better diversification and risk management. | | **Benefits for Advisors/Partners** | • Clear scope of responsibilities.
• Ability to bill for services.
• Compliance with regulatory frameworks. | In practice, when you see “mandate” in a system or API, it typically refers to a record that captures the client’s authorization status and the details of the relationship between the client and the financial service provider.
